key_insight: Nominally cubic CsGeBr3 hosts long-lived, one-dimensional polar chains despite having zero net polarization, while its ferroelectric phase switches polarization chain by chain.
engineering_relevance: These unusually slow, chain-mediated polarization dynamics could inform halide-perovskite switching models and device design.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics with first-principles-trained interatomic potentials.
Analysis of Ge off-centering, polar correlations, and relaxation dynamics.
Comparison with BaTiO3, PbTiO3, and CsSnBr3.
evidence_signal: Simulations show polar chains extending at least tens of nanometers and relaxing on nanosecond timescales—four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based findings; experimental validation and device-scale switching performance remain to be established.
paper_title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
